dyads.pattern_rationale: First preference question (Q01) is PE — Learner invites User to articulate general organising habit before execution begins. Subsequent PI questions (Q02, Q07, Q09) appear after the PE opener. Rule 2 applies.

questions.note: Pre-task. Asks how user generally organises the fridge (by drink preference or container type). User generates the preference content. PE despite raw code C1/Q2 — semantically elicits a general organising principle (per coding manual note on K11/C1 vs C4 inconsistency).

Learner proposes a generalizable layer-assignment rule (one layer for wine, one for drinks) and asks User to confirm. The hypothesis covers a zone/category and would apply to all items in those categories.

Single category (fruit) placement: top or bottom? AO.

Category placement query: where do opened food items go? Resolves a concrete zone assignment for a named category.
Learner proposes a generalizable rule: one layer for unopened items, one layer for opened items. Hypothesis covers all items of each type — generalizable if confirmed.

Declarative statement of arrangement plan (sides = wine and drinks; bottom = stacked neatly) rather than an explicit question. Functionally seeks implicit approval. Coded AO because no explicit generalizable rule is being validated; the question mark reflects the ambiguous interrogative status of this utterance.
Per the coding manual example: '只要开封了我就放第一层，可以吧' is a PI candidate. Learner proposes a rule: any opened item → first layer. The rule is generalizable (covers all opened items, not only named ones).
General 'Is this OK?' satisfaction check. Resolves acceptance of the overall arrangement outcome. No generalizable rule proposed.

Explicitly labeled 'summary of organising rules' in the JSON. Learner synthesises inferred rules (opened/unopened distinction + left=wine, right=drinks) and asks for validation. Classic PI per coding manual pattern: 'Summary check of inferred rules → PI'.
Proposes a generalizable rule: all unopened items → this layer. The scope is all future unopened items, not just the ones currently in hand.

dyads.pattern_rationale: First preference question (Q01) is PE — Learner opens with a general preference question about organising by type. Rule 2 applies. (Q09 is PI but appears after multiple PE questions; per coding manual Rule 1, pattern is determined by the first preference question.)

questions.note: Pre-task. '你一般喜欢所有东西按照种类放吗' — per coding manual example: 'PE'. Asks about general organising preference (by category). User generates the answer.
Pre-task. '你更喜欢横着摆放还是竖着？还是根据空间大小决定？' — asks about general orientation preference (horizontal vs. vertical or by space). Applies across multiple items. PE.

Pre-task. '现在的冰箱有什么你感觉不舒服的么' — elicits User's pain points with the current arrangement (implicit preference elicitation). User articulates what they dislike; the answer informs general organising goals. PE.
Pre-task. '基本规则是上面摆放的浅下面深吗？还是你更希望按照个人习惯' — asks User to choose between a general depth-placement rule or personal habit. Invites User to articulate a general depth-management preference. PE.
Pre-task. '这个冰箱比较高，你会把上面的空间也利用上吗，还是根据身高合适摆放' — asks about User's preference for vertical space utilisation. General preference question; User generates the answer. PE.

Pre-task. '在这个冰箱里，你使用频率最高的是什么东西？' — factual query about most frequently used items (K7). Supports placement decisions but does not elicit an organising principle — User states facts, not preferences. AO.
Pre-task. '你会经常用到食物嘛' — factual follow-up about food usage frequency. AO.
Pre-task. '零食吃的多吗？' — factual query about snack consumption frequency. AO.

Pre-task. Learner synthesises a full set of inferred organising rules (function-zone arrangement, infrequent items out of reach, drinks on the side, large-to-small) and asks User to validate: '这是这样吗'. Classic PI: Learner builds the preference model; User validates. Per coding manual: 'Summary check of inferred rules → PI'.
Pre-task. '对于冰箱深度，你会喜欢放在触手可及的地方，还是考虑摆放物体的稳定，比如放在外面会倒下来？' — asks User's preference on depth-placement strategy (accessibility vs. stability). User generates the answer. PE.
